title: Insights and the learning log
summary: Every answer is logged in detail, so the learner and the tutor can see what is hard.
description: How often the learner is wrong says little; what they find hard says a lot. The learner and the tutor read the same analysis.

stories.as: a learner who keeps making mistakes
stories.want: to see what kind they are and where they happen
stories.soThat: I know what to work on

stories.as: a learner asking the tutor for help
stories.want: the tutor to see the same analysis I can
stories.soThat: its advice fits what I actually get wrong

requirements.text: Every graded answer is written to the learning log in the same transaction as its grade.

Each wrong answer is given one mistake class, the most telling that fits: a sound contrast or preposition, Polish letters only, order only, an ending, a typo, a look-alike word when it was picked, some words right, or a word not known. A right answer typed without its Polish letters is classed as Polish letters too.
An answer's log row records the words it involved, including the words of a sentence and the wrong options shown beside it.
Log rows are append-only: never updated after they are written.
The Insights pages and the tutor's analysis tools use the same queries.

The raw log lists every answer and event, newest first, in pages of at most `log.page-max` rows, and can be filtered by item, course, lesson, exercise, mistake, topic, grammar, right or wrong, and period.
Words and sentences can be tagged with grammar structures and topics from lists built into the app; the tutor tags what it makes, and older content is tagged only when the learner asks.
A topic's numbers count toward its domain too.
The raw log can be exported as CSV or JSON, up to `log.export-max` rows.
A word's statistics can be broken down by context: the course, the role the word had, its grammatical context, the topic and the exercise.
